facts.fact: Snowflake Cortex AI is Snowflake's AI suite documented on the Cortex overview page (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/overview).

The Cortex overview page lists Cortex Agents, Cortex AI Functions (including LLM functions), Cortex Analyst, Cortex Fine-tuning, Cortex Search, Cortex Training, Snowflake CoWork, Cortex Code (Snowsight, CLI, Agent SDK, MCP, ACP, plugins) and Cortex AI Guardrails, and its sidebar also lists Cortex AI Gateway, Cortex Knowledge Extensions, Cortex Inference, AI Observability and Provisioned Throughput (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/overview).
Cortex Agents is listed as a feature of Snowflake Cortex AI on the Cortex overview page (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/overview).
Cortex AI Guardrails is listed as a feature of Snowflake Cortex AI on the Cortex overview page (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/overview).
Cortex Code (now Snowflake CoCo) is offered through Snowsight, a CLI, an Agent SDK, MCP, ACP and plugins (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/overview).

Snowflake Intelligence was renamed Snowflake CoWork, announced at Snowflake Summit 2026 on 2026-06-02, and current docs use 'Snowflake CoWork' (secondary) (https://itbrief.com.au/story/snowflake-renames-ai-tools-amid-broader-platform-push ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-cowork).

Some Snowflake CoWork object names still say SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE, for example the `SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS` schema and the `ALTER SNOWFLAKE INTELLIGENCE` command (secondary) (https://itbrief.com.au/story/snowflake-renames-ai-tools-amid-broader-platform-push ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-cowork).

Cortex Code was renamed Snowflake CoCo, announced 2026-06-02 at Summit 2026 alongside CoWork (secondary) (https://itbrief.com.au/story/snowflake-renames-ai-tools-amid-broader-platform-push ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cortex-code/cortex-code-cli).

Snowflake docs mix the names 'CoCo' and 'Cortex Code', and the CoCo CLI binary is still named `cortex` (secondary) (https://itbrief.com.au/story/snowflake-renames-ai-tools-amid-broader-platform-push ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cortex-code/cortex-code-cli).

Snowflake CoWork (formerly Snowflake Intelligence) is a conversational agentic application where business users query structured and unstructured data through Cortex Agents (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-cowork).

Snowflake CoWork is reached at `https://ai.snowflake.com`, while private connectivity uses a different URL (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-cowork/getting-started).
Snowflake CoWork uploads are limited to 5 files under 50 MB each (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-cowork).
Snowflake CoWork Deep Research runs take up to 10 minutes (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-cowork).
Snowflake CoWork document generation became GA on 2026-10-14 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).
Snowflake CoWork document generation requires the code execution tool on the agent (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-cowork).

If the account has a CoWork object (auto-created as `SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE_OBJECT_DEFAULT` on the first settings change), an agent must be added to it with `ALTER SNOWFLAKE INTELLIGENCE ...` to be visible in CoWork (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-cowork/deploy-agents).

Agents were historically made visible in CoWork by creating them in `SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS`, and docs describe a migration path from this schema method to the CoWork object (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-cowork/deploy-agents).

Cortex Agents orchestrate Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, Analytical search (public preview), code execution, Data to Chart, custom tools (stored procedures and UDFs), agent skills, MCP connectors, agent toolsets and web search (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).
Cortex Agents can orchestrate Cortex Analyst as a tool (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).
Cortex Agents can orchestrate Cortex Search as a tool (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).
The Cortex Agents Analytical search tool is in public preview as of 2026-11-14 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).
The Cortex Agents web search tool must be enabled at account level before agents can use it (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).

Snowflake recommends the `auto` orchestration model for Cortex Agents, which picks the highest-quality model available to the account; `models.orchestration` accepts a named model and `thinking_effort` controls reasoning effort (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-rest-api).
Cortex Agents examples set `models.orchestration` to the named model `claude-4-sonnet` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-rest-api).
Calling a Cortex Agent requires the `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` or `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_AGENT_USER` database role (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).
The `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_AGENT_USER` database role is an alternative to `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` for calling a Cortex Agent (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).
Calling a Cortex Agent also requires `USAGE` on the agent object plus privileges on every object its tools use (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).

Cortex Agents support threads, logs and traces, end-user feedback, agent evaluations, resource budgets on the agent object and per-user credit quotas (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-evaluations).

Cortex Agents orchestration and Cortex Analyst are charged per token, Cortex Search by index size and persistence time, and custom tools by warehouse compute, as of 2026-11-14 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).
Rates for Cortex Agents billing units are published in the Snowflake Service Consumption Table (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).

Cortex AI Functions (AISQL) are `AI_COMPLETE`, `AI_CLASSIFY`, `AI_FILTER`, `AI_AGG`, `AI_EMBED`, `AI_MULTI_EMBED`, `AI_EXTRACT`, `AI_SENTIMENT`, `AI_SUMMARIZE`, `AI_SUMMARIZE_AGG`, `AI_SIMILARITY`, `AI_TRANSCRIBE`, `AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT`, `AI_REDACT`, `AI_TRANSLATE`, plus helpers `TO_FILE`, `AI_COUNT_TOKENS` and `PROMPT` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql).
Some Cortex AI Functions are preview and the rest are GA as of 2026-11-14 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql).

facts.fact: Calling Cortex AI Functions requires the account-level `USE AI FUNCTIONS` privilege (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql).

Calling Cortex AI Functions requires either the `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` or the `SNOWFLAKE.AI_FUNCTIONS_USER` database role in addition to `USE AI FUNCTIONS` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql).
The `SNOWFLAKE.AI_FUNCTIONS_USER` database role is an alternative to `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` for calling Cortex AI Functions (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql).

Legacy `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.*` functions map to AI Functions: `COMPLETE`/`TRY_COMPLETE` to `AI_COMPLETE`, `CLASSIFY_TEXT` to `AI_CLASSIFY`, `EXTRACT_ANSWER` to `AI_EXTRACT`, `PARSE_DOCUMENT` to `AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT`, `EMBED_TEXT_768`/`EMBED_TEXT_1024` to `AI_EMBED`, `SENTIMENT`/`ENTITY_SENTIMENT` to `AI_SENTIMENT` and `COUNT_TOKENS` to `AI_COUNT_TOKENS`, and AI Functions are 'the focus of future development' (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql-migrate-legacy-functions).

Several legacy `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.*` to `AI_*` mappings change arguments or output, and no deprecation date for the legacy functions is stated (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql-migrate-legacy-functions).
`AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT` agentic mode entered public preview on 2026-10-28 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).
Page filtering for `AI_EXTRACT` and `AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT` was released on 2026-11-10 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).
`AI_TRANSCRIBE` received an accuracy update on 2026-11-13 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).
`AI_EXTRACT` is one of the Cortex AI Functions (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql).
The Claude models in the Snowflake Cortex model catalog are listed under Anthropic (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).

Snowflake Cortex GA Anthropic models are `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-5` and `claude-haiku-4-5` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).

In Snowflake Cortex, `claude-haiku-5-5` is in preview and `claude-fable-5-1` and `claude-fable-5` are in private preview as of 2026-11-14 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).

All Anthropic models in Snowflake Cortex are cross-region only except `claude-opus-4-6` and `claude-sonnet-4-6`, which are also native in AWS Europe West 2 (London) (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).
Claude 5.5 models became GA in Snowflake Cortex on 2026-11-06 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).
GPT-6 models became GA in Snowflake Cortex on 2026-11-06 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).
The GPT models in the Snowflake Cortex model catalog are listed under OpenAI (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).

Snowflake Cortex GA OpenAI models include `openai-gpt-6-astra`, `openai-gpt-6-sol`, `openai-gpt-6-luna`, `openai-gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna`, `openai-gpt-5.4` (plus `-mini` and `-nano` for AI Functions only), `openai-gpt-5.2`, `openai-gpt-5.1`, `openai-gpt-5`, `openai-gpt-5-mini` and `openai-gpt-5-nano` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).

`openai-gpt-6.1-sol` is GA for Inference, Agents and CoCo but private preview in AI Functions, `openai-gpt-6.1-terra` is preview and `openai-gpt-4.1` is legacy in Snowflake Cortex as of 2026-11-14 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).
Availability of `openai-gpt-5.6` and later models in Snowflake Cortex can vary by account (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).

In Snowflake Cortex, `gemini-4-argon` (GA 2026-11-03), `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash` and `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` are GA, while `gemini-3.1-pro` and `gemini-3.7-flash` are preview (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).

In Snowflake Cortex, Meta `llama3.3-70b` and `llama3.1-8b` are GA, while `llama4-maverick`, `llama3.1-70b`, `llama3-70b` and `llama3-8b` are legacy (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).
In Snowflake Cortex, `mistral-large3` is preview, while `mistral-large2`, `mixtral-8x7b` and `mistral-7b` are legacy (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).

The Snowflake Cortex catalog also has `deepseek-v4-flash` in private preview, Qwen3 models GA in AI Functions, and `kimi-k3`, `grok-4.7`, `grok-4.6` and `glm-5.3` in preview (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).

GA embedding models in Snowflake Cortex are `snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2.0-8k`, `snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2.0`, `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5`, `snowflake-arctic-embed-m`, `multilingual-e5-large`, `e5-base-v2`, `voyage-multilingual-2` and `nv-embed-qa-4` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).
Snowflake Cortex embedding models are native in many regions as well as available cross-region (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).

`SHOW CORTEX BASE MODELS IN SCHEMA SNOWFLAKE.MODELS` lists the Cortex models the current role can use, with release stage and cross-region scopes (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).
Legacy Cortex models remain callable until end-of-life only for accounts that already used them (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).
Cortex Search is managed hybrid (vector plus keyword) search over Snowflake text for RAG and agents (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).

A Cortex Search service is created with `CREATE CORTEX SEARCH SERVICE ... ON <col> ATTRIBUTES ... WAREHOUSE = ... TARGET_LAG = ... EMBEDDING_MODEL = ... AS (<query>)` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).
The default Cortex Search embedding model is `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).

Cortex Search supports multi-index services with `TEXT INDEXES` / `VECTOR INDEXES` and bring-your-own `VECTOR` columns (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).

Creating a Cortex Search service needs the `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` or `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_EMBED_USER` database role (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).

The `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_EMBED_USER` database role is an alternative to `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` for creating a Cortex Search service (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).

Creating a Cortex Search service needs `CREATE CORTEX SEARCH SERVICE` on the schema, `SELECT` on sources, `USAGE` on the warehouse and change tracking enabled (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).
Querying a Cortex Search service needs `USAGE` on the service, database and schema (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).
Suspending or resuming a Cortex Search service needs `OPERATE` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).

Cortex Search bills warehouse compute for refreshes, embedding tokens for added or changed rows, serving compute per GB per month of uncompressed indexed data, storage per TB and cloud services, as of 2026-11-14 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).
Cortex Search serving compute is charged even when the service receives no queries (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).

facts.fact: Staged YAML semantic model files remain in Cortex Analyst for backward compatibility (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst).

Snowflake now recommends Cortex Agents over Cortex Analyst, saying it 'supports every Cortex Analyst capability with higher answer quality' (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst).

Cortex Analyst model selection is not configurable: it uses the highest-ranked model the role can access in the order Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.5, OpenAI GPT 4.1, Arctic Text2SQL R1.5, Mistral Large 2 with Llama 3.1 70b, and requests fail if none is accessible (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst).
Using Cortex Analyst needs the `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` or the narrower `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_ANALYST_USER` database role (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst).
`SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_ANALYST_USER` is the narrower database role alternative to `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` for Cortex Analyst (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst).

Cortex Analyst needs `SELECT` on referenced tables, `READ` on the stage for YAML models and `USAGE` on any Cortex Search services used (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst).

Cortex Knowledge Extensions (CKE) are Cortex Search services shared by providers through Snowflake Marketplace, private or organizational listings (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-knowledge-extensions/cke-overview).

Cortex Knowledge Extensions are shared through Snowflake Marketplace or private or organizational listings (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-knowledge-extensions/cke-overview).

Consumers use Cortex Knowledge Extensions from AI Functions, Cortex Agents or CoWork, and a `SOURCE_URL` column enables citations (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-knowledge-extensions/cke-overview).

Usage-based billing is not supported for Cortex Knowledge Extensions, and CKEs cannot be used in listings with Egress Cost Optimizer (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-knowledge-extensions/cke-overview).
The Document AI UI and the `<model_build_name>!PREDICT` method were decommissioned on 2026-03-16 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/bcr-bundles/un-bundled/bcr-2156).
Document AI models not migrated to the Snowflake Model Registry are unavailable after the 2026-03-16 decommission (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/bcr-bundles/un-bundled/bcr-2156).

`AI_EXTRACT` replaces Document AI, with `AI_EXTRACT(model => ..., file => ...)` used for migrated legacy models (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/bcr-bundles/un-bundled/bcr-2156 ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/functions/ai_extract-document-ai).
`AI_EXTRACT` uses the model `arctic-extract` with token billing (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/functions/ai_extract-document-ai).

Cortex AI Gateway is one gateway object per account named `SNOWFLAKE` that gives coding agents, third-party clients and SDKs a single governed inference endpoint with traces, cost attribution, budgets and per-user quotas (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-ai-gateway).
`SHOW AI GATEWAYS;` finds the Cortex AI Gateway endpoint (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-ai-gateway).

facts.fact: Access to the Cortex AI Gateway is via the `USAGE` and `MONITOR` privileges (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-ai-gateway).
Cortex AI Gateway inference, observability and cost management became GA on 2026-11-03 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).

Cortex AI Gateway Tools (MCP) entered preview on 2026-10-19, and Trace analytics is in preview (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-ai-gateway ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).
The Snowflake CoCo (Cortex Code) CLI is an agentic coding CLI that orchestrates Snowflake skills and configured MCP tools (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cortex-code/cortex-code-cli).
The CoCo CLI uses `~/.snowflake/connections.toml`, shared with Snowflake CLI (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cortex-code/cortex-code-cli).
The CoCo CLI requires the `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` or `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_AGENT_USER` database role (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cortex-code/cortex-code-cli).
`SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_AGENT_USER` is an alternative to `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` for using the CoCo CLI (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cortex-code/cortex-code-cli).
The CoCo CLI is not available on standard trial accounts (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cortex-code/cortex-code-cli).
The Cortex Agent SDK is marked preview and available to all accounts as of 2026-11-14 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agent-sdk/sdk-features).

The Cortex Agent SDK is the TypeScript package `@snowflake/cortex-agent-sdk` and has the Python import root `cortex_agent_sdk` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agent-sdk/sdk-features).

The Cortex Agent SDK wraps inline and object agent runs (`api.agent.run`/`stream`/`create`), the managed coding agent (`api.coding_agent.run`) and CoCo sessions (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agent-sdk/sdk-features).
The Cortex Agent SDK can attach Snowflake MCP servers via `mcp_servers` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agent-sdk/sdk-features).
Cortex Training entered preview on 2026-10-30 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).
New Cortex fine-tuning model training was removed from AWS US East 1 on 2026-10-20 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).
Snowpark is a set of libraries for Python, Java and Scala that push DataFrame and UDF/stored-procedure code into Snowflake (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowpark/index).
The Snowpark Python package is `snowflake-snowpark-python`, with a `[pandas]` extra for pandas support (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowpark/python/setup).
Snowpark Python supports Python 3.10 to 3.14 as GA and Python 3.9 is deprecated (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowpark/python/setup).

Snowpark Container Services (SPCS) objects are an image repository (`CREATE IMAGE REPOSITORY`), compute pool, long-running service (`CREATE SERVICE`) and finite job service (`EXECUTE JOB SERVICE`) (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowpark-container-services/overview).
Snowpark Container Services is available in AWS, Azure and GCP commercial regions with some exceptions (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowpark-container-services/overview).
Outbound network access from Snowpark Container Services needs an external access integration (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowpark-container-services/overview).

Snowflake Native Apps are built from an application package (manifest file, setup script, versions and patches) and distributed via Marketplace or private listings (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/native-apps/native-apps-about).
Snowflake Native Apps can include SPCS containers (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/native-apps/native-apps-about).
Snowflake Native Apps can include Streamlit (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/native-apps/native-apps-about).
Cortex Agents and MCP servers inside Snowflake Native Apps became GA on 2026-08-07 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/2026/other/2026-08-07-native-apps-agents-mcp-ga).

facts.fact: Openflow is an Apache NiFi-based integration service (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-integration/openflow/about).
The Openflow Snowflake Deployment runs on SPCS (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-integration/openflow/about).
The Openflow Snowflake Deployment is GA in AWS, Azure and GCP commercial regions, and BYOC is GA in AWS commercial regions (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-integration/openflow/about).
New Openflow deployments are gen 2, and gen 2 connector configuration is in public preview as of 2026-11-14 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-integration/openflow/about).
Openflow is not auto-enabled on trial accounts (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-integration/openflow/about).
Openflow Endpoints became GA on 2026-10-16 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).

No Snowflake computer-use or browser-use agent capability was found; the closest are the Cortex Agents web search tool and the code execution tool (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).

The Snowflake-managed MCP server, a remote MCP server object created in the account, has been GA since 2025-11-04 after preview on 2025-10-02 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/2025/other/2025-11-04-cortex-agents-mcp).
The managed MCP server is a Snowflake-provided remote MCP server object (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/2025/other/2025-11-04-cortex-agents-mcp).
The managed MCP endpoint is `https://<account_url>/api/v2/databases/{database}/schemas/{schema}/mcp-servers/{name}` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).

A managed MCP server is created with `CREATE [OR REPLACE] MCP SERVER [IF NOT EXISTS] <name> FROM SPECIFICATION $$ <yaml> $$;` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).
Snowflake OAuth 2.0 is the default authentication for the managed MCP server (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).

External OAuth for the managed MCP server (for example Okta or Microsoft Entra ID via `OAUTH_AUTHORIZATION_SERVER`) and configurable scopes became GA on 2026-07-22 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/2026/other/2026-07-22-mcp-external-oauth).

A programmatic access token works with the managed MCP server, but Snowflake warns about token leakage and recommends a least-privileged role (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).
Dynamic client registration is not supported by the managed MCP server (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).

Managed MCP tool types are `CORTEX_AGENT_RUN`, `CODING_AGENT` (no stored agent object), `CORTEX_SEARCH_SERVICE_QUERY`, `CORTEX_ANALYST_MESSAGE` (semantic views only), `SYSTEM_EXECUTE_SQL` and `GENERIC` (UDFs and stored procedures) (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).
The managed MCP `CODING_AGENT` tool type was added on 2026-10-23, and background runs and extra agent tools were added on 2026-11-04 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).
Creating a managed MCP server needs `CREATE MCP SERVER` on the schema (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).
Updating a managed MCP server needs `OWNERSHIP` on it (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).

Connecting to and listing tools on a managed MCP server needs `USAGE` on the MCP server plus `USAGE` on the search services, agents and UDFs and `SELECT` on semantic views behind each tool (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).

The managed MCP server implements MCP revision 2025-11-25 tools only, with no resources, prompts, roots, notifications or sampling (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).
A managed MCP server allows at most 50 tools, and generic and SQL tool responses are truncated at 250 KB (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).

Since 2026-08-20 managed MCP `tools/call` responses are Server-Sent Events, so clients must accept both JSON and `text/event-stream` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).

The open-source `snowflake-labs-mcp` server (GitHub `Snowflake-Labs/mcp`) says 'This project is deprecated and no longer maintained'; secondary sources date the deprecation 2026-05-15 with last release v1.4.2 (https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/mcp ; (secondary) https://eseospace.com/blog/snowflake-mcp-server/).
The deprecated Snowflake Labs MCP server points users to the Snowflake-managed MCP server (https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/mcp).
The Snowflake Labs MCP server is run with `uvx snowflake-labs-mcp --service-config-file config.yaml` (https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/mcp).

The Snowflake Labs MCP server is configured by YAML with `agent_services`, `search_services`, `analyst_services` and `other_services` toggles for `object_manager`, `query_manager`, `semantic_manager`, and `sql_statement_permissions` (legacy reference) (https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/mcp).
The Snowflake Labs MCP server authenticates via the Python connector (password, key pair, OAuth, SSO, or PAT in the password field) or `--connection-name` (https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/mcp).
Cortex Agents can call external MCP servers through MCP connectors (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp-connectors).

To set up an MCP connector an admin creates an API integration with `API_PROVIDER = external_mcp` (auth `OAUTH2` with client ID/secret or `OAUTH_DYNAMIC_CLIENT` for DCR) and a `CREATE EXTERNAL MCP SERVER ... URL ... API_INTEGRATION` object, then adds it to the agent spec (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp-connectors ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/create-api-integration).

Cortex Agents MCP connectors support OAuth only, with callback `https://identity.snowflake.com/oauth2/callback` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp-connectors).

Cortex Agents MCP connectors support tools only and include prebuilt connectors for Atlassian, GitHub, Glean, Linear and Salesforce (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp-connectors).
Cortex Agents expose a REST API for agent object CRUD and runs (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-rest-api).

Cortex Agents object CRUD uses `POST|GET /api/v2/databases/{db}/schemas/{schema}/agents` and `GET|PUT|DELETE .../agents/{name}`, with body fields `profile`, `models`, `instructions`, `orchestration` (including `budget.seconds`/`budget.tokens`), `tools`, `tool_resources` and `thinking_effort` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-rest-api).

facts.fact: Cortex Agents run endpoints are object run `POST /api/v2/databases/{db}/schemas/{schema}/agents/{name}:run`, inline run `POST /api/v2/cortex/agent:run`, stream `GET /api/v2/cortex/agent/runs/{run_id}` and cancel `POST /api/v2/cortex/agent/runs/{run_id}/cancel` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-run).

The Cortex Agents run body accepts `thread_id`, `parent_message_id`, `messages`, `background`, `stream` (default true), `tool_choice` (`auto`, `required`, `tool`) and `client_metadata` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-run).

Cortex Agents API tool type identifiers are `cortex_analyst_text_to_sql` (one of `semantic_model_file` or `semantic_view`), `cortex_search` (`search_service`, `id_column`, `title_column`, `filter`), `generic` (UDF or procedure via `tool_resources` with `execution_environment` type `warehouse`), `web_search` (`max_results`) and `system_execute_sql` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-rest-api ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-run).

Cortex Agents SSE events are `response.status`, `response.thinking.delta`, `response.text.delta`, `response.text.annotation`, `response.tool_use`, `response.tool_result`, `response.table`, `response.chart`, `response.map`, `response.warning`, `metadata`, `error` and a final `response` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-run).
Cortex Agents API clients must tolerate unknown SSE event types (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-run).

Cortex Agents threads persist conversation state for runs via `thread_id` and `parent_message_id`, documented on the Threads API page (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-threads-rest-api).

Threads are required for Cortex Agents background runs (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-threads-rest-api ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-run).

The Cortex REST API base is `https://<account-identifier>.snowflakecomputing.com/api/v2/cortex/v1` with `/chat/completions` (OpenAI-compatible, all models), `/messages` (Anthropic-compatible, Claude only) and `/responses` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-rest-api).
The Cortex REST API `/responses` endpoint (OpenAI-compatible, OpenAI models on AWS) has been in preview since 2026-10-23 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features).
Calling the Cortex REST API requires the default role to have `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` or `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_REST_API_USER` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-rest-api).

`SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_REST_API_USER` is an alternative to `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER` on the default role for calling the Cortex REST API (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-rest-api).
The Cortex REST API is Snowflake's inference API hosted on the account URL (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-rest-api).

Cortex Analyst exposes `POST /api/v2/cortex/analyst/message` taking `messages` and one of `semantic_view`, `semantic_model_file`, `semantic_model` (inline YAML) or `semantic_models` (array) (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst/rest-api).

With `stream: true` the Cortex Analyst REST API returns SSE events `status`, `message.content.delta`, `error`, `warnings`, `response_metadata` and `done` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst/rest-api).

Cortex Search is queried with `POST https://<account_url>/api/v2/databases/<db>/schemas/<schema>/cortex-search-services/<service>:query` taking `query`, `columns`, `filter` (`@eq`, `@contains`, `@gte`, `@lte`, `@primarykey`, `@and`, `@or`, `@not`), `scoring_config`/`scoring_profile` and `limit` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/query-cortex-search-service).
The Cortex Search query `limit` defaults to 10 with a maximum of 1000 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/query-cortex-search-service).
Cortex Search can be previewed from SQL via `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SEARCH_PREVIEW` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/query-cortex-search-service).
The Snowflake REST APIs are GA as of 2026-11-14 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/snowflake-rest-api).
The Snowflake REST APIs are OpenAPI-compliant resource APIs (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/snowflake-rest-api).

Snowflake REST APIs live at `https://<organization>-<account>.snowflakecomputing.com/api/v2/<resource>` for accounts, users, roles, grants, warehouses, databases, schemas, tables, stages, pipes, tasks, SPCS compute pools/services, functions, procedures, secrets, network policies, integrations, notebooks, Streamlit and Cortex Embed/Inference/Search (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/snowflake-rest-api).
Snowflake REST API specs are in the `snowflake-rest-api-specs` GitHub repo (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/snowflake-rest-api).

Snowflake REST APIs accept `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with `X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type: KEYPAIR_JWT`, where the JWT is valid at most 1 hour (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/authentication).
Snowflake REST APIs accept OAuth bearer tokens with `X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type: OAUTH` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/authentication).
Snowflake REST APIs accept PAT bearer tokens with `X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type: PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/authentication).

Snowflake REST APIs accept `X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type: WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_FEDERATION` with bearer `WIF.{AWS|AZURE|GCP|OIDC}.{token}` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/authentication).

The Snowflake SQL API endpoint `/api/v2/statements` submits SQL, checks status, fetches partitioned results and cancels statements (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/sql-api/intro ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/sql-api/index).
The Snowflake SQL API supports OAuth authentication (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/sql-api/intro).
The Snowflake SQL API supports key pair authentication (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/sql-api/intro).

The Snowflake SQL API does not support `PUT`/`GET`, and `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`, `USE`, `ALTER SESSION`, session variables and temp tables/stages work only in multi-statement requests (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/sql-api/intro).

`pip install snowflake` installs the unified Snowflake Python package, with resource management in `snowflake.core` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-python-api/snowflake-python-overview).
`snowflake.core` is GA and supports Python 3.10 to 3.14 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-python-api/snowflake-python-overview).

The Snowflake Python APIs manage databases, warehouses, tasks, SPCS, Cortex services and more without SQL (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-python-api/snowflake-python-overview).

facts.fact: Official Snowflake drivers are JDBC, ODBC, Snowflake Connector for Python, Node.js, Go, .NET and PHP PDO (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/drivers).
Snowflake ODBC driver 4.x is GA and built on Universal Core (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/drivers).
The Snowflake Connector for Python is built on Universal Core, a shared Rust library (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/drivers).
All official Snowflake drivers support TLS 1.2 and 1.3 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/drivers).
The Snowflake .NET driver on macOS lacks TLS 1.3 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/drivers).
The Python package `snowflake-connector-python` is at 5.2.0 and requires Python >=3.11 (https://pypi.org/pypi/snowflake-connector-python/json).
The Node.js npm package `snowflake-sdk` is at 3.4.1 and requires Node >=20 (https://registry.npmjs.org/snowflake-sdk/latest).
The Go driver `github.com/snowflakedb/gosnowflake/v2` v2.0.0 was released 2026-03-03 and requires Go 1.25+ (https://github.com/snowflakedb/gosnowflake).

The Snowflake JDBC driver is Maven `net.snowflake:snowflake-jdbc`, also available as `snowflake-jdbc-fips` and `snowflake-jdbc-thin` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/jdbc/jdbc-download).

Recommended Snowflake client versions are JDBC 4.4.0+, ODBC 4.2.0+, Python connector 5.2.0+, Node.js 3.4.1+, Go 2.3.0+, .NET 6.5.0+, Snowflake CLI 3.18.0+ and Snowpark Python 1.44.0+ (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/requirements).

Minimum Snowflake client versions as of 2026-10-27 are JDBC 3.20.0, Python 3.12.4, Node 1.15.0 and Go 1.12.0 (ODBC 3.5.0 and .NET 4.2.0 as of 2026-10-02), and versions below minimum may be blocked (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/requirements).

Egress is set up with `CREATE NETWORK RULE ... MODE = EGRESS TYPE = HOST_PORT VALUE_LIST = (...)`, `CREATE SECRET` (for example `TYPE = OAUTH2` or `GENERIC_STRING`) and `CREATE EXTERNAL ACCESS INTEGRATION ... ALLOWED_NETWORK_RULES ... ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATION_SECRETS ... ENABLED = TRUE`, then referenced with `EXTERNAL_ACCESS_INTEGRATIONS` and `SECRETS` on UDFs/procedures (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/external-network-access/creating-using-external-network-access).
Creating an external access integration needs `CREATE INTEGRATION` on the account (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/external-network-access/creating-using-external-network-access).

Openflow connectors cover SharePoint, Google Drive, Box, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server, MongoDB, Kafka, Kinesis, Salesforce Bulk API, Slack, Jira Cloud, Workday, Shopify, HubSpot, Microsoft Dataverse, Veeva Vault and ad platforms (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-integration/openflow/about).
Agent-side MCP connectors cover Atlassian, GitHub, Glean, Linear and Salesforce (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp-connectors).
The CoCo CLI supports the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/overview).
No Snowflake A2A (Agent2Agent) support was found (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/overview).
Snowflake Agent, Analyst and inference APIs stream via SSE (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-run).
No general outbound webhook product was researched for this note, so Snowflake event delivery beyond SSE is unconfirmed (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-run).

On Windows, Snowflake CLI (`snow`) installs via the PowerShell standalone installer `irm https://sfc-repo.snowflakecomputing.com/snowflake-cli/install.ps1 | iex`, the MSI `snowflake-cli-<version>-x86_64.msi` from the Snowflake CLI repository, or Python tools (`pipx install snowflake-cli`, `uv tool install snowflake-cli`, `pip install snowflake-cli`; Python 3.11+) (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/installation/installation).
winget is not listed as an install method for Snowflake CLI (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/installation/installation).
The latest PyPI release of `snowflake-cli` is 3.33.0, uploaded 2026-11-09 (https://pypi.org/pypi/snowflake-cli/json).

`snow --version` verifies the Snowflake CLI version, and `snow upgrade` (standalone) or `uv tool upgrade snowflake-cli` upgrades it (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/installation/installation).

Snowflake CLI uses `--config-file` first, otherwise `config.toml` in `SNOWFLAKE_HOME` or `~/.snowflake` if that directory exists, otherwise the OS default, on Windows `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\snowflake\config.toml`; `snow --info` shows `default_config_file_path` and Windows logs are at `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\snowflake\logs` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-cli).

`connections.toml` must sit beside `config.toml` and uses bare `[name]` sections; if both define connections only `connections.toml` is read while `default_connection_name` is still read from `config.toml`, and `--config-file` does not move where `connections.toml` is read (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-connections ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-cli).

Snowflake CLI sign-in commands are `snow connection add` (interactive or with flags and `--no-interactive`), `snow connection test -c <name>`, `snow connection list`, `snow connection set-default <name>`, and `-x/--temporary-connection` for flag-only use (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-connections).

facts.fact: Snowflake CLI authenticators are `SNOWFLAKE` (password plus `--mfa-passcode`), `USERNAME_PASSWORD_MFA`, `SNOWFLAKE_JWT` (key pair), `OAUTH`, `OAUTH_AUTHORIZATION_CODE`, `OAUTH_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS`, `EXTERNALBROWSER`, `PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN` (`token_file_path`) and `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-connections).
Snowflake CLI supports key pair authentication with authenticator `SNOWFLAKE_JWT` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-connections).

Snowflake CLI supports OAuth with authenticators `OAUTH`, `OAUTH_AUTHORIZATION_CODE` and `OAUTH_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-connections).
Snowflake CLI supports authenticator `PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN` with `token_file_path` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-connections).

Snowflake CLI supports authenticator `WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` with `workload_identity_provider` = `AWS`, `AZURE`, `GCP` or `OIDC` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-connections).

`SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTIONS_<NAME>_<KEY>` overrides a key in an existing Snowflake CLI connection (it does not create one); precedence is CLI flags, then those env vars, then file connections, then generic vars like `SNOWFLAKE_USER`, and `SNOWFLAKE_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_NAME` selects the default (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-connections).

Snowflake CLI command groups are `ai`, `app`, `bootstrap`, `connection`, `cortex`, `custom-image`, `dbt`, `dcm`, `feedback`, `git`, `helpers`, `logs`, `notebook`, `object`, `snowpark`, `spcs`, `sql`, `stage`, `streamlit` and `upgrade` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/command-reference/overview).
`snow cortex complete|extract-answer|sentiment|summarize|translate` call Cortex functions (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/command-reference/cortex-commands/overview).

Preview commands `snow ai claude` and `snow ai opencode` launch the local Claude Code or OpenCode agent with model traffic routed through Cortex AI Gateway using the selected CLI connection (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/command-reference/ai-commands/overview).
`snow ai claude` (preview) launches the local Claude Code agent routed through Cortex AI Gateway (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/command-reference/ai-commands/overview).
`snow ai opencode` (preview) launches the local OpenCode agent routed through Cortex AI Gateway (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/command-reference/ai-commands/overview).
The preview `snow ai` commands are hidden from `snow --help` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/command-reference/ai-commands/overview).
Snowflake docs say 'SnowSQL is a legacy command-line client' and only Snowflake CLI gets new features (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowsql-migrate).
SnowSQL 1.5.x is supported through 2028-04-16 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowsql-migrate).
Snowflake CLI replaces the legacy SnowSQL client (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowsql-migrate).

Migrate from SnowSQL with `snow helpers import-snowsql-connections` and `snow helpers check-snowsql-env-vars`, and alias it in PowerShell with `function snowsql { snow sql @args }` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowsql-migrate).

Moving from SnowSQL to `snow sql`, `--config` becomes `--config-file`, `-o output_format` becomes `--format json`, piped input needs `--stdin`, and variables use `-D x=1` with `<% x %>` (SnowSQL `&x` deprecated) (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowsql-migrate).

On Windows, `irm https://ai.snowflake.com/static/cc-scripts/install.ps1 | iex` installs the CoCo `cortex` executable to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cortex` and adds it to PATH; it works natively or via WSL (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cortex-code/cortex-code-cli).

The Terraform provider `snowflakedb/snowflake` (repo `snowflakedb/terraform-provider-snowflake`) manages Snowflake resources, with example auth `authenticator = SNOWFLAKE_JWT` plus `private_key` (https://registry.terraform.io/v1/providers/snowflakedb/snowflake ; https://github.com/snowflakedb/terraform-provider-snowflake).
The latest Snowflake Terraform provider is v2.23.0, published 2026-11-05 (https://registry.terraform.io/v1/providers/snowflakedb/snowflake).
The Snowflake Terraform provider requires Terraform 1.1.5+ (https://github.com/snowflakedb/terraform-provider-snowflake).

Only v2.0.0+ stable resources of the Snowflake Terraform provider are officially supported, preview resources need `preview_features_enabled`, and OpenTofu is not supported (https://github.com/snowflakedb/terraform-provider-snowflake).
Snowflake REST APIs support `CREATE OR ALTER` semantics for infrastructure-as-code style management (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/snowflake-rest-api).
The Snowflake Python APIs (`snowflake.core`) manage Snowflake resources declaratively from Python (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/snowflake-rest-api).

Snowflake CLI has a `dcm` command group and project definition files (unverified that `dcm` means Database Change Management) (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/command-reference/overview).
The Snowflake docs root `https://docs.snowflake.com/` resolves with the title 'Snowflake Documentation' (https://docs.snowflake.com/).

The Cortex AI overview `https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/overview` resolves and links all Cortex features (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/overview).

`https://docs.snowflake.com/llms.txt` exists and indexes per-section `llms.txt` files (for example `https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/llms.txt`), pages are available as `.md` by appending `.md`, and no `llms-full.txt` is listed (https://docs.snowflake.com/llms.txt ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/llms.txt).
No official Snowflake documentation MCP server was found, only community projects (secondary) (https://lobehub.com/en/mcp/sfc-gh-miwhitaker-mcp-snowdocs).
The model availability page is the canonical Cortex model list by product, stage and region (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/model-availability).

Snowflake server feature releases are at `https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features`, behavior change bundles under `/en/release-notes/bcr-bundles/`, and client versions at `/en/release-notes/requirements` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/new-features ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/requirements).

facts.fact: The status page `https://status.snowflake.com/` shows per-region component status across AWS, Azure and GCP with email, SMS, Slack, Teams and webhook subscriptions (https://status.snowflake.com/).
OpenAPI specs for the Snowflake REST APIs are in GitHub `snowflake-rest-api-specs` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/snowflake-rest-api).

The Cortex AI Cookbook docs section has recipes such as LangChain agents on Cortex AI Gateway with MCP tools and multi-agent orchestration with a CoWork profile (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/cortex-ai-cookbook/langchain-mcp-agent-tracing).
A Cortex AI Cookbook recipe runs LangChain agents on Cortex AI Gateway with MCP tools (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/cortex-ai-cookbook/langchain-mcp-agent-tracing).

Cortex REST API rate limits are per account per model in RPM and TPM, for example `claude-sonnet-4-6` 6,000,000 TPM / 10,000 RPM and `openai-gpt-5` 600,000 TPM / 600 RPM, with HTTP 429 when exceeded; cross-region inference raises some limits and `CORTEX_REST_API_RATE_LIMIT_POLICIES` shows them (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-rest-api).

Cortex REST API `max_completion_tokens` defaults to 4,096 (theoretical max 131,072, per-model caps apply), with 20 images per conversation and a 20 MiB max request (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-rest-api).

Long Cortex REST API requests return HTTP 503 'inference timed out', and expired session tokens return HTTP 200 with error code 390112 (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-rest-api).

Cortex Agents REST requests time out after 15 minutes, background runs (`background: true`, threads required) time out after 6 hours, and `client_metadata` is at most 4096 bytes (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-run).
Cortex Agents background runs are available on AWS and Azure only (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-run).

Cortex Agents run events are streamable only while the run is active and up to 5 minutes after completion, after which the API returns 409 Conflict (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-run).
Cortex Agents APIs cannot be called from Streamlit in Snowflake apps on a warehouse runtime; use the container runtime (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents).

Cortex Search allows 20 QPS per service and 140 QPS per account (raise via account team), a source query under 400M rows, recommended chunks of at most 512 tokens and a REST response max of 10 MB (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/query-cortex-search-service).

Cortex Search services cannot be cloned, and source tables should not be altered while the service is running (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-search/cortex-search-overview).
Most Cortex models are cross-region only, so using them depends on cross-region inference (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cross-region-inference).

Account parameter `CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION` (values `DISABLED`, `ANY_REGION`, or region groups such as `AWS_US`, `AWS_EU`, `AZURE_EU`, `GCP_US`) governs cross-region inference and is set only by `ACCOUNTADMIN` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cross-region-inference ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/parameters).
Cortex cross-region inference is not available in China (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cross-region-inference).

Under BCR 2026_06 (bcr-2376), commercial accounts that never set `CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION` now default to a same-cloud geography (for example `AWS_US`, `AWS_EU`, `AZURE_US`, `GCP_US`), generally enabled (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/bcr-bundles/2026_06/bcr-2376 ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/parameters).

New accounts in new orgs created after 2026-03-09 get `CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION = ANY_REGION`, while finance, healthcare, government, FedRAMP and VPS accounts and some regions (for example AWS sa-east-1) remain `DISABLED` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/bcr-bundles/2026_06/bcr-2376).

`CORTEX_MODELS_ALLOWLIST` (default `'All'`) can only be changed to `'None'` from August 2026 and will be removed later in 2026; use model-level RBAC instead (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/parameters).

`STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS` defaults to 172800 (2 days) with max 604800 (7 days), is settable at account, user, session and warehouse with the lowest non-zero value winning, and `STATEMENT_QUEUED_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS` defaults to 0 (no timeout) (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/parameters).

MCP server objects are not replicated in failover groups and must be recreated on the secondary, although OAuth security integrations do replicate (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).
The managed MCP server is not available in Azure US Gov Virginia non-FedRAMP-High and is not yet FedRAMP assessed (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).

External MCP connectors are OAuth only, refresh token validity must be at least 3600 seconds if set (0 means never expires), hostnames must use hyphens not underscores, and disabling the API integration immediately invalidates user tokens (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp-connectors).

Service users (`TYPE=SERVICE` or `LEGACY_SERVICE`) need a network policy to generate or use a PAT and human users need one to authenticate with it, while `TYPE=SERVICE_AGENT` users do not (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/programmatic-access-tokens).
Snowflake PATs default to 15-day expiry with a maximum of 365 days (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/programmatic-access-tokens).

Service users must set `ROLE_RESTRICTION` for PATs, the PAT secret is shown only once, and `LOGIN_NAME` must be used as the user when passing a PAT as password (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/programmatic-access-tokens).

facts.fact: The `CORTEX_ANALYST_MESSAGE` managed MCP tool works with semantic views only, not YAML semantic model files (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-agents-mcp).

The Snowflake SQL API has no `PUT`/`GET`, allows transaction and session commands only in multi-statement requests, and Python/Java/Scala procedures returning Arrow resultsets can error (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/sql-api/intro).

On macOS/Linux the Snowflake CLI `config.toml` must be owner read/write only (`chmod 0600`) or the CLI errors, and `SF_SKIP_TOKEN_FILE_PERMISSIONS_VERIFICATION=true` downgrades `0644` to a warning (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-connections).
If `SNOWFLAKE_HOME` points to a missing directory the Snowflake CLI does not fall back to `~/.snowflake` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli/connecting/configure-cli).
The CoCo CLI is not available on standard trial accounts (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cortex-code/cortex-code-cli).
On trial accounts Openflow must be enabled by the account team (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-integration/openflow/about).
Snowflake Intelligence was renamed Snowflake CoWork on 2026-06-02 (secondary for rename date) (https://itbrief.com.au/story/snowflake-renames-ai-tools-amid-broader-platform-push).
Cortex Code was renamed Snowflake CoCo on 2026-06-02 (secondary for rename date) (https://itbrief.com.au/story/snowflake-renames-ai-tools-amid-broader-platform-push).
The Document AI UI and `!PREDICT` were retired 2026-03-16 in favor of `AI_EXTRACT` (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/bcr-bundles/un-bundled/bcr-2156).
`SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.*` functions are superseded by `AI_*` functions (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql-migrate-legacy-functions).

The Snowflake Labs MCP server is deprecated in favor of the Snowflake-managed MCP server (https://itbrief.com.au/story/snowflake-renames-ai-tools-amid-broader-platform-push ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/bcr-bundles/un-bundled/bcr-2156 ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql-migrate-legacy-functions).

SnowSQL is legacy in favor of Snowflake CLI (https://itbrief.com.au/story/snowflake-renames-ai-tools-amid-broader-platform-push ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/release-notes/bcr-bundles/un-bundled/bcr-2156 ; https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/aisql-migrate-legacy-functions).
